chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A woman shortens her hair for her Umrah by the measure of a fingernail.
ai.seo_question: How much hair should a woman cut during Umrah?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the distinction between men's complete shaving (tahalluq) and women's partial trimming (taqseer) during Umrah. The specific measure of 'anmulah' (the length of a fingernail) reflects the juristic consensus that women are exempt from the full ritual shaving required of men, emphasizing a proportional act of completion. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh, ensuring the ritual is accessible while maintaining its symbolic significance of leaving the state of ihram.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Taqseer for a woman from her hair for her Umrah, is to be of the measurement of a finger-nail’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of our people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Taqsir (cutting some hair or finger nails and so on) in the case of women is from her hairs of the size of a finger tip.’”
